source.text: Τότε προσηνέχθη αὐτῷ δαιμονιζόμενος τυφλὸς καὶ κωφός· καὶ ἐθεράπευσεν αὐτόν, ὥστε τὸν κωφὸν λαλεῖν καὶ βλέπειν.

records.literal_gloss: Then was brought to him a demon-possessed blind and mute; and he healed him, so that the mute to speak and to see.

en.L: Then a demon-possessed [man], blind and mute, was brought to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} healed him, so that the mute [man] spoke and saw.
en.B: Then a man under the power of a demon was brought to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. The man was blind and unable to speak. Jesus healed him, and now the man could speak and see.
en.R: Then some people brought a man to Jesus. A demon was controlling the man, and he was blind and could not talk. Jesus healed him, and the man was able to talk and to see.

es.L: Entonces {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} fue traído un endemoniado, ciego y mudo; y lo sanó, de modo que el mudo hablaba y veía.
es.B: Entonces {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} trajeron a un hombre que estaba bajo el poder de un demonio. Era ciego y no podía hablar. Jesús lo sanó, y el hombre pudo hablar y ver.
es.R: Entonces algunas personas le llevaron un hombre a Jesús. Un demonio controlaba al hombre, y él era ciego y no podía hablar. Jesús lo sanó, y el hombre pudo hablar y ver.

sw.L: Kisha akaletewa mtu mwenye pepo, kipofu na bubu; {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} akamponya, kiasi kwamba yule bubu alisema na kuona.
sw.B: Kisha mtu mmoja aliyekuwa chini ya nguvu za pepo aliletwa {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}. Mtu huyo alikuwa kipofu, tena hakuweza kusema. Yesu akamponya, na sasa mtu huyo akaweza kusema na kuona.
sw.R: Kisha watu fulani walimleta mtu mmoja kwa Yesu. Pepo alikuwa akimtawala mtu huyo, naye alikuwa kipofu na hakuweza kuongea. Yesu akamponya, na mtu huyo akaweza kuongea na kuona.

decisions.choice: demon-possessed: under a demon's control
decisions.reason: As in 9:32-33, Matthew links the man's blindness and muteness with the demon.

decisions.choice: mute: unable to speak
decisions.reason: The word can mean deaf or mute. Here it means mute, since healing lets him speak.

decisions.choice: some people brought
decisions.reason: Readable makes the passive active.

decisions.choice: endemoniado (L); bajo el poder de un demonio (B); un demonio lo controlaba (R)
decisions.reason: As the term sheet settles for the whole New Testament, "demonio" names these spirits; "diablo" is kept for Satan himself (12:26). Balanced and Readable say what being possessed meant (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: mwenye pepo (L); chini ya nguvu za pepo (B); pepo alikuwa akimtawala (R)
decisions.reason: As the term sheet settles for the whole New Testament, "pepo" names these spirits; "Shetani" is kept for Satan himself (12:26). Balanced and Readable say what being possessed meant (meaning decision m1).

source.text: καὶ ἐξίσταντο πάντες οἱ ὄχλοι καὶ ἔλεγον· Μήτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱὸς Δαυίδ;

records.literal_gloss: And were amazed all the crowds and were saying, Not this is the son of David?

en.L: And all the crowds were amazed and were saying, "This is not the Son of David, is it?"
en.B: The crowds were all beside themselves. "Might this man be the Son of David?" they asked.
en.R: All the people were amazed. They said, "Could this man be the Son of David, the king God promised?"

es.L: Y se asombraban todas las multitudes y decían: «¿Acaso es este el Hijo de David?».
es.B: Toda la gente estaba fuera de sí. «¿Será este el Hijo de David?», se preguntaban.
es.R: Toda la gente estaba asombrada. Decían: «¿Podría ser este hombre el Hijo de David, el rey que Dios prometió?».

sw.L: Na makutano wote wakashangaa, wakawa wakisema, "Huyu si Mwana wa Daudi, au sivyo?"
sw.B: Makutano wote wakastaajabu kupita kiasi. Wakauliza, "Je, yawezekana huyu ndiye Mwana wa Daudi?"
sw.R: Watu wote walishangaa. Wakasema, "Je, inawezekana mtu huyu ndiye Mwana wa Daudi, mfalme aliyeahidiwa na Mungu?"

decisions.choice: a hesitant question
decisions.reason: The question is framed as if expecting "no", but it shows that the crowds are beginning to wonder.

decisions.choice: Son of David: a title for the promised king
decisions.reason: As in 9:27, the title names the Messiah (1:1).

decisions.choice: the king God promised
decisions.reason: Readable says what the title means.

decisions.choice: ¿Acaso es...? (L); ¿Será...? (B); ¿Podría ser...? (R)
decisions.reason: The question is hesitant (meaning decision m1): the crowd half expects the answer no but wonders. Spanish "acaso" and the future of guessing ("¿Será...?") carry that doubt without English's tag "is it?".

decisions.choice: Je, yawezekana...? (B); Je, inawezekana...? (R)
decisions.reason: The question is hesitant (meaning decision m1): the crowd half expects the answer no but wonders. "Yawezekana" (could it be) carries that doubt; Literal keeps the Greek's shape with a tag question, as the English Literal does.

source.text: οἱ δὲ Φαρισαῖοι ἀκούσαντες εἶπον· Οὗτος οὐκ ἐκβάλλει τὰ δαιμόνια εἰ μὴ ἐν τῷ Βεελζεβοὺλ ἄρχοντι τῶν δαιμονίων.

records.literal_gloss: The but Pharisees having heard said, This one not casts out the demons except by the Beelzebul ruler of the demons.

en.L: But when the Pharisees heard [it], they said, "This [man] does not cast out the demons except by Beelzebul, [the] ruler of the demons."
en.B: But the Pharisees heard it and said, "This man drives out demons only with the help of Beelzebul, the prince of demons."
en.R: But the Pharisees heard what the people were saying. They said, "This man makes demons leave only by the power of Beelzebul. Beelzebul is the ruler of the demons."

es.L: Pero los fariseos, oyendo [esto], dijeron: «Este no echa fuera los demonios sino por Beelzebul, [el] príncipe de los demonios».
es.B: Pero los fariseos lo oyeron y dijeron: «Este expulsa los demonios solo con la ayuda de Beelzebul, el jefe de los demonios».
es.R: Pero los fariseos oyeron lo que decía la gente. Dijeron: «Este hombre hace salir a los demonios solo por el poder de Beelzebul. Beelzebul es el jefe de los demonios».

sw.L: Lakini Mafarisayo waliposikia [hayo], wakasema, "Huyu hatoi pepo isipokuwa kwa Beelzebuli, mkuu wa pepo."
sw.B: Lakini Mafarisayo waliposikia hivyo wakasema, "Mtu huyu anafukuza pepo kwa msaada wa Beelzebuli tu, mkuu wa pepo."
sw.R: Lakini Mafarisayo walisikia watu walichokuwa wakisema. Wakasema, "Mtu huyu anawatoa pepo kwa nguvu za Beelzebuli tu. Beelzebuli ndiye mtawala wa pepo."

decisions.choice: Beelzebul: a name for Satan
decisions.reason: Jesus answers the charge as one about Satan (12:26). The name recalls Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron (2 Kings 1:2), and Jesus has already said that his opponents call him Beelzebul (10:25).

decisions.choice: Beelzebul, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Some early Greek manuscripts spell the name Beezebul. The form Beelzebub, familiar from older translations, comes from the Latin and Syriac traditions and 2 Kings 1:2. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: by: by the power of
decisions.reason: The Pharisees say Satan is the power at work in Jesus.

source.text: εἰδὼς δὲ τὰς ἐνθυμήσεις αὐτῶν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Πᾶσα βασιλεία μερισθεῖσα καθ’ ἑαυτῆς ἐρημοῦται, καὶ πᾶσα πόλις ἢ οἰκία μερισθεῖσα καθ’ ἑαυτῆς οὐ σταθήσεται.

records.literal_gloss: Having known but the thoughts of them he said to them, Every kingdom divided against itself is laid waste, and every city or house divided against itself not will stand.

en.L: But knowing their thoughts, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Every kingdom divided against itself is laid waste, and every city or household divided against itself will not stand.
en.B: Jesus knew what they were thinking, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Any kingdom that is split into warring parts falls into ruin, and any town or family that fights against itself will not last.
en.R: Jesus knew what they were thinking. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "A kingdom that fights against itself will be destroyed. A town or a family that fights against itself will fall apart.

es.L: Pero conociendo sus pensamientos, les dijo: «Todo reino dividido contra sí mismo queda devastado, y toda ciudad o familia dividida contra sí misma no se sostendrá.
es.B: Jesús sabía lo que estaban pensando, y les dijo: «Cualquier reino dividido en bandos enfrentados termina en ruinas, y cualquier pueblo o familia que pelea contra sí mismo no durará.
es.R: Jesús sabía lo que estaban pensando. Por eso les dijo: «Un reino que pelea contra sí mismo será destruido. Un pueblo o una familia que pelea contra sí misma se vendrá abajo.

sw.L: Lakini akiyajua mawazo yao, akawaambia, "Kila ufalme uliogawanyika dhidi yake wenyewe huharibiwa kabisa, na kila mji au jamaa iliyogawanyika dhidi yake yenyewe haitasimama.
sw.B: Yesu aliyajua mawazo yao, akawaambia, "Ufalme wowote uliogawanyika katika makundi yanayopigana huanguka na kuwa magofu, na mji wowote au jamaa yoyote inayojipiga yenyewe haitadumu.
sw.R: Yesu alijua walichokuwa wakifikiri. Kwa hiyo akawaambia, "Ufalme unaopigana wenyewe kwa wenyewe utaangamizwa. Mji au familia inayopigana yenyewe kwa yenyewe itasambaratika.

decisions.choice: knowing their thoughts: as in 9:4
decisions.reason: Jesus knows what they think, as God knows the heart.

decisions.choice: house: a household or family
decisions.reason: The word means the people who live together in a house.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Jesus's answer begins a long speech, so Balanced and Readable name him.

decisions.choice: familia
decisions.reason: The word means a household or family (meaning decision m2); Spanish "casa" could be read as the building.

decisions.choice: jamaa (L, B); familia (R)
decisions.reason: The word means a household or family (meaning decision m2); "nyumba" would be read as the building.

source.text: καὶ εἰ ὁ Σατανᾶς τὸν Σατανᾶν ἐκβάλλει, ἐφ’ ἑαυτὸν ἐμερίσθη· πῶς οὖν σταθήσεται ἡ βασιλεία αὐτοῦ;

records.literal_gloss: And if the Satan the Satan casts out, against himself he is divided; how then will stand the kingdom of him?

en.L: And if Satan casts out Satan, he is divided against himself; how then will his kingdom stand?
en.B: So if Satan is throwing Satan out, he has turned against himself. In that case, how could his kingdom survive?
en.R: If Satan forces out his own demons, then he is fighting against himself. How could his kingdom last?

es.L: Y si Satanás echa fuera a Satanás, contra sí mismo está dividido; ¿cómo, pues, se mantendrá su reino?
es.B: Así que, si Satanás expulsa a Satanás, se ha puesto en contra de sí mismo. En ese caso, ¿cómo podría sobrevivir su reino?
es.R: Si Satanás expulsa a sus propios demonios, entonces está peleando contra sí mismo. ¿Cómo podría durar su reino?

sw.L: Na kama Shetani anamtoa Shetani, amegawanyika dhidi yake mwenyewe; basi ufalme wake utasimamaje?
sw.B: Basi ikiwa Shetani anamfukuza Shetani, amejigeuka dhidi yake mwenyewe. Kama ni hivyo, ufalme wake ungewezaje kudumu?
sw.R: Kama Shetani anawafukuza pepo wake mwenyewe, basi anajipiga vita yeye mwenyewe. Ufalme wake ungewezaje kudumu?

decisions.choice: Satan casting out Satan: Satan driving out his own servants
decisions.reason: If the demons are Satan's servants, driving them out would mean Satan fighting himself.

decisions.choice: his own demons
decisions.reason: Readable says what the second "Satan" means.

source.text: καὶ εἰ ἐγὼ ἐν Βεελζεβοὺλ ἐκβάλλω τὰ δαιμόνια, οἱ υἱοὶ ὑμῶν ἐν τίνι ἐκβάλλουσιν;

records.literal_gloss: And if I by Beelzebul cast out the demons, the sons of you by whom do they cast out?

en.L: And if I cast out the demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons cast [them] out?
en.B: And if I drive out demons with Beelzebul's help, then whose help do your own people use when they drive them out?
en.R: You say that I force out demons by the power of Beelzebul. Then by whose power do your own followers force them out?

es.L: Y si yo echo fuera los demonios por Beelzebul, ¿por quién [los] echan fuera {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} hijos?
es.B: Y si yo expulso a los demonios con la ayuda de Beelzebul, ¿con la ayuda de quién los expulsa {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} propia gente?
es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes dicen|Vosotros decís}} que yo hago salir a los demonios por el poder de Beelzebul. Entonces, ¿con el poder de quién los hacen salir {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} propios seguidores?

sw.L: Na ikiwa {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} natoa pepo kwa Beelzebuli, wana wenu huwatoa kwa nani?
sw.B: Na kama {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} nawafukuza pepo kwa msaada wa Beelzebuli, je, watu wenu wenyewe huwafukuza kwa msaada wa nani?
sw.R: Mnasema kwamba {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} nawafukuza pepo kwa nguvu za Beelzebuli. Basi wafuasi wenu wenyewe huwafukuza kwa nguvu za nani?

decisions.choice: your sons: your own people, your followers
decisions.reason: "Sons" can mean members or followers of a group. Some Jews of the time drove out demons (Acts 19:13).

decisions.choice: your own people (B); your own followers (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means.

decisions.choice: You say that
decisions.reason: Jesus takes up the Pharisees' own claim; Readable says so.

decisions.choice: ustedes / vosotros forms
decisions.reason: Jesus answers the Pharisees as a group, so every plural "you" and its verb in 12:25-37 is the reader setting: ustedes (Latin America, the default) or vosotros (Spain).

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}
decisions.reason: As in John: when Jesus speaks of himself, the free pronoun "mimi" takes the deity_pronoun setting in Swahili, though the English "I" has none. The pronouns marked inside the verb are written plain.

source.text: διὰ τοῦτο αὐτοὶ κριταὶ ἔσονται ὑμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Because of this they judges will be of you.

en.L: Because of this, they will be your judges.
en.B: So they will be the ones to judge you.
en.R: So your own followers will show that you are wrong.

es.B: Así que ellos mismos serán quienes {{plural_you:los|os}} juzguen.
es.R: Así que {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} propios seguidores demostrarán que {{plural_you:están|estáis}} equivocados.

sw.L: Kwa sababu hiyo, wao watakuwa waamuzi wenu.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo wafuasi wenu wenyewe wataonyesha kwamba mmekosea.

decisions.choice: judges: they will show that your charge is false
decisions.reason: Their own exorcists show the charge to be unfair, and so they condemn it.

decisions.choice: will show that you are wrong
decisions.reason: Readable says how they will judge.

source.text: εἰ δὲ ἐν πνεύματι θεοῦ ἐγὼ ἐκβάλλω τὰ δαιμόνια, ἄρα ἔφθασεν ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: If but by Spirit of God I cast out the demons, then has come upon you the kingdom of the God.

en.L: But if I cast out the demons by [the] Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.
en.B: But if I am driving out demons by the Spirit of God, then God's kingdom has already arrived among you.
en.R: But suppose I am forcing out demons by the power of God's Spirit. That means God's kingdom has come to you.

es.L: Pero si yo echo fuera los demonios por [el] Espíritu de Dios, entonces ha llegado a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} el reino de Dios.
es.B: Pero si expulso a los demonios por el Espíritu de Dios, entonces el reino de Dios ya ha llegado hasta {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.R: Pero supongamos que yo hago salir a los demonios por el poder del Espíritu de Dios. Eso quiere decir que el reino de Dios ha llegado a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.

sw.L: Lakini kama {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} nawatoa pepo kwa Roho wa Mungu, basi ufalme wa Mungu umewafikia.
sw.B: Lakini kama nawafukuza pepo kwa Roho wa Mungu, basi ufalme wa Mungu tayari umefika kwenu.
sw.R: Lakini tuseme nawafukuza pepo kwa nguvu za Roho wa Mungu. Hiyo inamaanisha kwamba ufalme wa Mungu umewafikia.

decisions.choice: has come upon you: has already arrived
decisions.reason: The verb means to arrive or reach. Elsewhere the kingdom "has come near" (3:2; 4:17); here Jesus says it is already at work among them.

decisions.choice: the kingdom of God: Matthew's usual "kingdom of heaven" in other words
decisions.reason: Matthew nearly always says "kingdom of heaven", but here and in a few other places "kingdom of God" (19:24; 21:31, 43).

decisions.choice: by the Spirit of God: the Spirit God put on his servant
decisions.reason: The quotation in 12:18 said God would put his Spirit on his servant (see 3:16).

source.text: ἢ πῶς δύναταί τις εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν τοῦ ἰσχυροῦ καὶ τὰ σκεύη αὐτοῦ ἁρπάσαι, ἐὰν μὴ πρῶτον δήσῃ τὸν ἰσχυρόν;

records.literal_gloss: Or how is able anyone to enter into the house of the strong and the goods of him to plunder, if not first he binds the strong?

en.L: Or how can anyone enter the house of the strong [man] and plunder his goods, unless he first binds the strong [man]?
en.B: Or how could anyone break into the house of a strong man and make off with his goods, without tying the strong man up first?
en.R: Suppose someone wants to go into a strong man's house and take away his things. First he must tie up the strong man.

es.L: ¿O cómo puede alguien entrar en la casa del fuerte y saquear sus bienes, si primero no ata al fuerte?
es.B: ¿O cómo podría alguien meterse en la casa de un hombre fuerte y llevarse sus cosas sin haber atado primero al hombre fuerte?
es.R: Supongamos que alguien quiere entrar en la casa de un hombre fuerte y llevarse sus cosas. Primero tiene que atar al hombre fuerte.

sw.L: Au mtu yeyote anawezaje kuingia katika nyumba ya [mtu] mwenye nguvu na kunyakua vitu vyake, kama hajamfunga kwanza yule mwenye nguvu?
sw.B: Au mtu angewezaje kuvunja na kuingia katika nyumba ya mtu mwenye nguvu na kuchukua mali yake, bila kumfunga kwanza mtu huyo mwenye nguvu?
sw.R: Tuseme mtu anataka kuingia katika nyumba ya mtu mwenye nguvu na kuchukua vitu vyake. Kwanza lazima amfunge yule mtu mwenye nguvu.

decisions.choice: the strong man: Satan; binding him: Jesus overpowering him
decisions.reason: Jesus pictures his casting out of demons as the defeat of Satan. Isaiah 49:24-25 asks whether captives can be taken from the mighty, and God answers that they will be.

decisions.choice: his goods: the people Satan has held captive
decisions.reason: In the picture, the goods taken from the strong man are those Jesus sets free.

decisions.choice: a statement instead of a question
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer "no one"; Readable states the point.

source.text: καὶ τότε τὴν οἰκίαν αὐτοῦ διαρπάσει.

records.literal_gloss: And then the house of him he will plunder.

en.L: And then he will plunder his house.
en.B: Only then can he strip the house bare.
en.R: Then he can take everything in the house.

es.B: Solo entonces podrá dejar la casa vacía.
es.R: Entonces puede llevarse todo lo que hay en la casa.

sw.B: Hapo tu ndipo anaweza kuipora nyumba yote.
sw.R: Kisha anaweza kuchukua kila kitu kilichomo ndani ya nyumba.

decisions.choice: and then: only after the strong man is bound
decisions.reason: The order matters: the binding comes first, then the plundering.

source.text: ὁ μὴ ὢν μετ’ ἐμοῦ κατ’ ἐμοῦ ἐστιν, καὶ ὁ μὴ συνάγων μετ’ ἐμοῦ σκορπίζει.

records.literal_gloss: The not being with me against me is, and the not gathering with me scatters.

en.L: The one who is not with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and the one who does not gather with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} scatters.
en.B: Anyone who does not stand with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} stands against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. Anyone who does not help {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} gather is scattering.
en.R: If people are not on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} side, they are against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. If they do not help {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} bring people together, they are driving people away.

es.L: El que no está conmigo, está contra {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}; y el que no reúne conmigo, dispersa.
es.B: Quien no se pone de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} lado se pone en contra de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. Quien no {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ayuda a recoger está dispersando.
es.R: Los que no están de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} lado están en contra de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. Los que no {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ayudan a reunir a la gente la están alejando.

sw.L: Asiyekuwa pamoja {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} ananipinga, na asiyekusanya pamoja {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} anatawanya.
sw.B: Mtu yeyote asiyesimama upande {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} anasimama dhidi {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. Mtu yeyote asiyenisaidia kukusanya anatawanya.
sw.R: Kama watu hawako upande {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, wako kinyume {{deity_pronoun:changu|Changu}}. Kama hawanisaidii kuwaleta watu pamoja, wanawafukuza watu mbali.

decisions.choice: gather, scatter: the picture of a flock or a harvest
decisions.reason: Jesus gathers God's scattered sheep (9:36-38; Ezekiel 34:12-13). Those who do not help him work against him.

decisions.choice: no neutral ground
alternatives: a rebuke for the disciples only
decisions.reason: In the fight between God's kingdom and Satan's, no one can stand aside.

decisions.choice: bring people together
decisions.reason: Readable says what is gathered.

decisions.choice: conmigo, with no span
decisions.reason: "Conmigo" is one word, "with me", and is written plain, as in John; the other pronouns for Jesus (mí, mi, me) take the deity_pronoun setting as the English does.

source.text: διὰ τοῦτο λέγω ὑμῖν, πᾶσα ἁμαρτία καὶ βλασφημία ἀφεθήσεται τοῖς ἀνθρώποις, ἡ δὲ τοῦ πνεύματος βλασφημία οὐκ ἀφεθήσεται.

records.literal_gloss: Because of this I say to you, every sin and blasphemy will be forgiven to men, the but of the Spirit blasphemy not will be forgiven.

en.L: Because of this I tell you, every sin and blasphemy will be forgiven to {{gender:people|men}}, but the blasphemy [against] the Spirit will not be forgiven.
en.B: This is why I tell you that people can be forgiven every sin and every slander, but no one will be forgiven for blasphemy against the Spirit.
en.R: So I tell you this: God will forgive people for every sin and for every evil thing they say against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. But God will not forgive anyone who speaks evil against the Holy Spirit.

es.L: Por esto {{plural_you:les|os}} digo: todo pecado y blasfemia les será perdonado {{gender:a las personas|a los hombres}}, pero la blasfemia [contra] el Espíritu no será perdonada.
es.B: Por eso {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que a la gente se le puede perdonar todo pecado y toda calumnia, pero a nadie se le perdonará la blasfemia contra el Espíritu.
es.R: Por eso {{plural_you:les|os}} digo esto: Dios perdonará a la gente todo pecado y todo lo malo que digan contra {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Pero Dios no perdonará a nadie que hable mal contra el Espíritu Santo.

sw.L: Kwa ajili ya hayo nawaambia, kila dhambi na kufuru itasamehewa kwa wanadamu, lakini kufuru [dhidi ya] Roho haitasamehewa.
sw.B: Ndiyo sababu nawaambia kwamba watu wanaweza kusamehewa kila dhambi na kila kashfa, lakini hakuna atakayesamehewa kwa kumkufuru Roho.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo nawaambia hivi: Mungu atawasamehe watu kila dhambi na kila neno baya wanalosema dhidi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. Lakini Mungu hatamsamehe mtu yeyote anayesema mabaya dhidi ya Roho Mtakatifu.

decisions.choice: blasphemy against the Spirit: calling the Spirit's work in Jesus the work of Satan
alternatives: any careless word about the Spirit
decisions.reason: The saying answers the charge of 12:24. Jesus drives out demons by the Spirit of God (12:28), and the Pharisees call it Satan's work (see Mark 3:30).

decisions.choice: blasphemy: slander, especially against God
decisions.reason: The word means speaking evil of someone. Most often in the Bible it is speech against God.

decisions.choice: will be forgiven: by God
decisions.reason: The passive points to God as the one who forgives.

decisions.choice: God will forgive; the Holy Spirit
decisions.reason: Readable names who forgives and which Spirit is meant (12:32).

decisions.choice: wanadamu, with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English Literal offers "men" as the traditional alternative to "people" here and in 12:35-36. "Wanadamu" and "mtu" already mean anyone, man or woman, so Swahili needs no span.

source.text: καὶ ὃς ἐὰν εἴπῃ λόγον κατὰ τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου, ἀφεθήσεται αὐτῷ· ὃς δ’ ἂν εἴπῃ κατὰ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἁγίου, οὐκ ἀφεθήσεται αὐτῷ οὔτε ἐν τούτῳ τῷ αἰῶνι οὔτε ἐν τῷ μέλλοντι.

records.literal_gloss: And whoever if speaks a word against the Son of the Man, it will be forgiven him; whoever but speaks against the Spirit the Holy, not it will be forgiven him neither in this the age nor in the coming.

en.L: And whoever speaks a word against the Son of Man, it will be forgiven him; but whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit, it will not be forgiven him, neither in this age nor in the [age] to come.
en.B: A person who says something against the Son of Man may be forgiven. But a person who speaks against the Holy Spirit will find no forgiveness, not in the present age and not in the age that is coming.
en.R: People who say something bad against the Son of Man can be forgiven. But people who speak against the Holy Spirit will never be forgiven. They will not be forgiven now or in the time to come.

es.L: Y quien diga una palabra contra el Hijo del Hombre, se le perdonará; pero quien hable contra el Espíritu Santo, no se le perdonará, ni en esta era ni en la [era] que viene.
es.B: A quien diga algo contra el Hijo del Hombre se le podrá perdonar. Pero quien hable contra el Espíritu Santo no hallará perdón, ni en la era presente ni en la era que está por venir.
es.R: A las personas que digan algo malo contra el Hijo del Hombre se les puede perdonar. Pero a las que hablen contra el Espíritu Santo nunca se les perdonará. No serán perdonadas ni ahora ni en el tiempo que vendrá.

sw.L: Na yeyote atakayesema neno dhidi ya Mwana wa Adamu, atasamehewa; lakini yeyote atakayesema dhidi ya Roho Mtakatifu, hatasamehewa, wala katika zama hizi wala katika [zama] zijazo.
sw.B: Mtu anayesema jambo dhidi ya Mwana wa Adamu anaweza kusamehewa. Lakini mtu anayesema dhidi ya Roho Mtakatifu hatapata msamaha, si katika zama hizi za sasa wala katika zama zinazokuja.
sw.R: Watu wanaosema jambo baya dhidi ya Mwana wa Adamu wanaweza kusamehewa. Lakini watu wanaosema dhidi ya Roho Mtakatifu hawatasamehewa kamwe. Hawatasamehewa sasa wala katika wakati ujao.

decisions.choice: against the Son of Man, against the Spirit: misjudging Jesus can be forgiven; calling God's plain work evil shuts out forgiveness
alternatives: the Spirit is greater than the Son
a sin a believer may commit by accident
decisions.reason: People may misjudge Jesus in his humble state and later turn. Those who see the Spirit's work and call it Satan's refuse the very forgiveness God offers. The saying is hard, and its exact scope is debated.

decisions.choice: neither in this age nor in the coming one: never
decisions.reason: Jews of the time spoke of this age and the age to come. To say "neither" is to say "never".

decisions.choice: never; now or in the time to come
alternatives: in this age or the coming age
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning and keeps the two times.

decisions.choice: era (L, B)
decisions.reason: As in Galatians 1:4: in modern Spanish "siglo" is a century and "mundo" would suggest the created world; "era" keeps the sense of a period of history. Readable says "never", "now or in the time to come", as the English does (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: zama (L, B)
decisions.reason: As in Galatians 1:4: "zama" is an age, a period of history; "ulimwengu" would mean the world. Readable says "kamwe" (never), "now or in the time to come", as the English does (meaning decision m2).

source.text: Ἢ ποιήσατε τὸ δένδρον καλὸν καὶ τὸν καρπὸν αὐτοῦ καλόν, ἢ ποιήσατε τὸ δένδρον σαπρὸν καὶ τὸν καρπὸν αὐτοῦ σαπρόν· ἐκ γὰρ τοῦ καρποῦ τὸ δένδρον γινώσκεται.

records.literal_gloss: Either make the tree good and the fruit of it good, or make the tree bad and the fruit of it bad; by for the fruit the tree is known.

en.L: Either make the tree good and its fruit good, or make the tree rotten and its fruit rotten; for by the fruit the tree is known.
en.B: Either count the tree good and its fruit good, or count the tree rotten and its fruit rotten. For the fruit shows what kind of tree it is.
en.R: A good tree gives good fruit, and a bad tree gives bad fruit. You cannot have it both ways. People know what a tree is like by looking at its fruit.

es.L: O {{plural_you:hagan|haced}} el árbol bueno y su fruto bueno, o {{plural_you:hagan|haced}} el árbol podrido y su fruto podrido; pues el árbol se conoce por el fruto.
es.B: O {{plural_you:consideren|considerad}} bueno el árbol y bueno su fruto, o {{plural_you:consideren|considerad}} podrido el árbol y podrido su fruto. Porque el fruto muestra qué clase de árbol es.
es.R: Un árbol bueno da fruto bueno, y un árbol malo da fruto malo. No se pueden tener las dos cosas a la vez. La gente sabe cómo es un árbol mirando su fruto.

sw.L: Ama mfanye mti uwe mwema na tunda lake jema, ama mfanye mti uwe mbovu na tunda lake bovu; kwa kuwa kwa tunda mti hujulikana.
sw.B: Ama mhesabu mti kuwa mzuri na tunda lake kuwa zuri, ama mhesabu mti kuwa mbovu na tunda lake kuwa bovu. Kwa maana tunda huonyesha mti ni wa aina gani.
sw.R: Mti mzuri huzaa matunda mazuri, na mti mbaya huzaa matunda mabaya. Hamwezi kusema yote mawili. Watu hujua mti ulivyo kwa kuangalia matunda yake.

decisions.choice: make: count, judge to be
decisions.reason: Jesus asks them to judge consistently. A good deed such as setting a man free cannot come from an evil source.

decisions.choice: the tree is known by its fruit: as in 7:16-20
decisions.reason: Jesus used the same picture of false prophets. Here it applies both to his own deeds and to the Pharisees' words (12:34-37).

decisions.choice: rotten: bad, worthless
decisions.reason: The word means rotten and so useless.

decisions.choice: You cannot have it both ways
decisions.reason: Readable says what "either ... or" demands.

source.text: γεννήματα ἐχιδνῶν, πῶς δύνασθε ἀγαθὰ λαλεῖν πονηροὶ ὄντες;

records.literal_gloss: Offspring of vipers, how are you able good things to speak evil being?

en.L: Offspring of vipers! How can you speak good things, being evil?
en.B: You family of snakes! How could good words come from you, since you are evil?
en.R: You are like a family of poisonous snakes! You are evil, so how can you say good things?

es.L: ¡Crías de víboras! ¿Cómo {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} hablar cosas buenas, siendo malos?
es.B: ¡Familia de serpientes! ¿Cómo podrían salir palabras buenas de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, si {{plural_you:son|sois}} malos?
es.R: ¡{{plural_you:Son|Sois}} como una familia de serpientes venenosas! {{plural_you:Son|Sois}} malos, así que ¿cómo {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} decir cosas buenas?

sw.L: Enyi watoto wa nyoka wa sumu! Mnawezaje kusema mambo mema, nanyi ni waovu?
sw.B: Ninyi ukoo wa nyoka! Maneno mema yangewezaje kutoka kwenu, ilhali ninyi ni waovu?
sw.R: Ninyi ni kama ukoo wa nyoka wenye sumu! Ninyi ni waovu, kwa hiyo mnawezaje kusema mambo mema?

decisions.choice: offspring of vipers: John the Baptist's words (3:7)
decisions.reason: Jesus uses John's words for the leaders. The wording is the same as in 3:7 at each level.

decisions.choice: crías de víboras (L)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is offspring, the young of an animal; "generación" now means people of the same age. The same words as John the Baptist's in 3:7 (meaning decision m1).

source.text: ἐκ γὰρ τοῦ περισσεύματος τῆς καρδίας τὸ στόμα λαλεῖ.

records.literal_gloss: Out of for the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks.

en.L: For out of the overflow of the heart the mouth speaks.
en.B: The mouth speaks what spills over from the heart.
en.R: What people say shows what is in their hearts.

es.L: Porque la boca habla de lo que rebosa del corazón.
es.B: La boca dice lo que se desborda del corazón.
es.R: Lo que la gente dice muestra lo que hay en su corazón.

sw.L: Kwa maana kinywa hunena kutokana na wingi wa moyo.
sw.B: Kinywa husema yale yanayofurika kutoka moyoni.
sw.R: Maneno ya watu huonyesha kilichomo mioyoni mwao.

decisions.choice: heart: the inner self, where thoughts and choices begin
decisions.reason: In the Bible the heart is the center of a person's thinking and will.

decisions.choice: What people say shows what is in their hearts
alternatives: out of the overflow of the heart the mouth speaks
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of the proverb plainly.

source.text: ὁ ἀγαθὸς ἄνθρωπος ἐκ τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ θησαυροῦ ἐκβάλλει ἀγαθά, καὶ ὁ πονηρὸς ἄνθρωπος ἐκ τοῦ πονηροῦ θησαυροῦ ἐκβάλλει πονηρά.

records.literal_gloss: The good man out of the good treasure brings out good things, and the evil man out of the evil treasure brings out evil things.

en.L: The good {{gender:person|man}} out of the good treasure brings out good things, and the evil {{gender:person|man}} out of the evil treasure brings out evil things.
en.B: From a good storehouse a good person draws out good things; from an evil storehouse an evil person draws out evil things.
en.R: Good people have good things stored in their hearts, so they bring out good things. Evil people have evil things stored in their hearts, so they bring out evil things.

es.L: {{gender:La persona buena|El hombre bueno}}, del buen tesoro, saca cosas buenas; y {{gender:la persona mala|el hombre malo}}, del mal tesoro, saca cosas malas.
es.B: De un buen depósito, una persona buena saca cosas buenas; de un depósito malo, una persona mala saca cosas malas.
es.R: Las personas buenas tienen cosas buenas guardadas en el corazón, y por eso sacan cosas buenas. Las personas malas tienen cosas malas guardadas en el corazón, y por eso sacan cosas malas.

sw.L: Mtu mwema hutoa vitu vyema kutoka katika hazina njema, na mtu mwovu hutoa vitu viovu kutoka katika hazina mbaya.
sw.B: Mtu mwema hutoa vitu vyema kutoka katika ghala lake la mema; mtu mwovu hutoa vitu viovu kutoka katika ghala lake la maovu.
sw.R: Watu wema wana mambo mema yaliyohifadhiwa mioyoni mwao, kwa hiyo hutoa mambo mema. Watu waovu wana mambo maovu yaliyohifadhiwa mioyoni mwao, kwa hiyo hutoa mambo maovu.

decisions.choice: treasure: a storehouse, here the heart
decisions.reason: The word means a treasure or the place where it is kept. The heart is meant (12:34; 6:21).

decisions.choice: stored in their hearts
decisions.reason: Readable says what the storehouse is.

decisions.choice: tesoro (L); depósito (B)
decisions.reason: The word is a storehouse as well as what is stored in it (meaning decision m1). Spanish "tesoro" suggests only riches; Balanced says "depósito", where things are kept and brought out, as the English says "storehouse".

decisions.choice: hazina (L); ghala (B)
decisions.reason: The word is a storehouse as well as what is stored in it (meaning decision m1). "Hazina" suggests riches; Balanced says "ghala", a store from which things are brought out, as the English says "storehouse".

source.text: λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι πᾶν ῥῆμα ἀργὸν ὃ λαλήσουσιν οἱ ἄνθρωποι, ἀποδώσουσιν περὶ αὐτοῦ λόγον ἐν ἡμέρᾳ κρίσεως·

records.literal_gloss: I say but to you that every word careless which will speak men, they will give about it an account in day of judgment;

en.L: But I tell you that every careless word that {{gender:people|men}} will speak, they will give an account of it on [the] day of judgment.
en.B: And I tell you this: every idle word people speak is a word they will have to answer for on judgment day.
en.R: I tell you that on the day when God judges people, they will have to explain every careless word they have said.

es.L: Pero {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que de toda palabra descuidada que pronuncien {{gender:las personas|los hombres}}, rendirán cuenta en [el] día del juicio.
es.B: Y {{plural_you:les|os}} digo esto: de cada palabra inútil que diga la gente tendrá que responder en el día del juicio.
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo que en el día en que Dios juzgue a la gente, todos tendrán que explicar cada palabra descuidada que hayan dicho.

sw.L: Lakini nawaambia kwamba kila neno la bure watakalolisema wanadamu, watalitolea hesabu katika siku ya hukumu.
sw.B: Nami nawaambia hivi: kila neno la ovyo ambalo watu husema ni neno watakalolazimika kulijibia siku ya hukumu.
sw.R: Nawaambia kwamba siku ile Mungu atakapowahukumu watu, watalazimika kueleza kila neno la ovyo walilosema.

decisions.choice: careless: idle, useless, spoken without thought
decisions.reason: The word means idle or useless. Even words spoken without care show what is in the heart.

decisions.choice: give an account: answer for, as before a judge
decisions.reason: The phrase is used of settling accounts and of answering for one's actions.

decisions.choice: the day when God judges people
decisions.reason: Readable says who judges.

source.text: ἐκ γὰρ τῶν λόγων σου δικαιωθήσῃ, καὶ ἐκ τῶν λόγων σου καταδικασθήσῃ.

records.literal_gloss: By for the words of you you will be justified, and by the words of you you will be condemned.

en.L: For by your words you will be justified, and by your words you will be condemned."
en.B: Your own words will declare you innocent, or your own words will condemn you."
en.R: The words you say will show whether you are right with God or guilty before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

es.L: Pues por tus palabras serás declarado justo, y por tus palabras serás condenado».
es.B: Tus propias palabras te declararán inocente, o tus propias palabras te condenarán».
es.R: Las palabras que dices mostrarán si estás bien con Dios o si eres culpable ante {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}».

sw.L: Kwa kuwa kutokana na maneno yako utatangazwa kuwa mwenye haki, na kutokana na maneno yako utahukumiwa kuwa na hatia."
sw.B: Maneno yako mwenyewe yatakutangaza kuwa huna hatia, au maneno yako mwenyewe yatakuhukumu."
sw.R: Maneno unayosema yataonyesha kama uko sawa mbele za Mungu au una hatia mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}."

decisions.choice: justified: declared in the right at the judgment
decisions.reason: The verb is set against "condemned", so it means acquitted by the judge.

decisions.choice: your: singular
decisions.reason: Jesus turns to each person: every one will answer for his or her own words.

decisions.choice: declare you innocent (B); right with God (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what being justified means here.

decisions.choice: tus, singular, with no plural_you span
decisions.reason: Jesus turns from the group to each hearer: "your" is singular here (meaning decision m2), so Spanish uses "tú" forms and there is no ustedes / vosotros setting in this sentence.

decisions.choice: utatangazwa kuwa mwenye haki (L)
decisions.reason: The verb means to be declared in the right at the judgment (meaning decision m1), so Literal says "declared" in so many words. The singular "yako" keeps the Greek's turn to each hearer (m2).
